messages:
maya: Heads-up — staging p99 jumped from ~18ms to ~42ms after the 3:10am rollout (model v2.3 onboarding). Noticed cold-starts and KV cache warmup looks wrong. Anyone watching kernels/batching?

jon: saw alerts. repro locally on a single GPU with the new checkpoint. Quick grep shows tokenizer offsets changed in the onboard script commit 3f8a2d7. Could that change seq lengths?

sasha: @jon yep — tokenizer now forces add_prefix_space=True and normalizes offsets. That causes different token boundaries for some prompts; avg token count up ~20% for our benchmark set.

lucas: increased tokens -> affects kernel selection heuristics. Profiling trace:
```
KERNEL_SELECT: seq_len=256, batch=1 -> chosen_kernel=attn_block_unfused (latency_path=slow)
PREV_BASELINE: seq_len=210, batch=4 -> chosen_kernel=attn_fused_v1 (fast)
PERF: p50=11ms p95=28ms p99=42ms (current)
BASELINE: p50=9ms p95=16ms p99=18ms (before)
```
Looks like kernel selector switched to unfused attention because observed seq_len distribution changed. Also batching heuristics started sending smaller batches (batch=1 more frequently).

maya: CI perf job also failed on the onboarding gate: ci-bot posted p95 regress of 1.7x for v2.3.

ci-bot: perf-ci: failure for commit 3f8a2d7 on linux-gpu-rt. Test: perf/onboard_latency. p95 increased from 15ms -> 26ms. See job 2026-03-18T03:14Z.

jon: ran bisect across onboard commits, narrowed to 3f8a2d7 (tokenizer offset normalization). Repro script: `python infra/tools/perf_profile.py --model v2.3 --promptset smoke --trace-kernel` reproduces kernel path flip.

ops: is KV cache being invalidated per request? That could cause warmup spikes. Any logs?

lucas: checked logs, kvcache hits drop from ~95% -> ~62% in early requests for same client id. Stack: tokenizer producing different token ids, so prefix matching misses cause cache bypasses. Snippet:
```
KV_HIT_RATE: client=staging-1 window=first_30s -> 0.62
KV_HIT_RATE: baseline client=staging-1 window=first_30s -> 0.95
```

maya: That explains cold token expansion + kernel misroute + lower batching. All amplifies p99. Any quick mitigation?

sasha: We have two short options: 1) revert 3f8a2d7 (tokenizer change) in onboarding pipeline to restore tokenization & caching behavior; 2) force kernel selection override for this model to prefer attn_fused_v1 for small batches until we fix tokenizer mapping detection. Option 1 is simplest.

jon: I can open a revert PR and a targeted rollout stop for v2.3. Will also add a regression test that compares token counts across onboarding runs.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated: reverting 3f8a2d7 -> PR #1427. Stopping further rollouts for v2.3.

ci-bot: perf-ci: re-run on revert PR #1427 queued.

maya: thumbs up. Action items: revert PR merge, add token-count equality check to onboarding CI, add a temporary kernel-override flag in runtime for v2.3 as a safety net, and follow-up to make tokenizer changes backwards compatible.

lucas: I'll add a quick kernel-override feature-flag (config key: runtime.kernel_override.prefer_fused) scoped to project/model to ops config.

ops: once revert passes perf-ci and staging looks good, we'll promote to prod with canary.

jon: notes for postmortem: root cause = tokenizer config drift in onboarding script causing tokenization divergence -> KV prefix misses -> batching contraction + kernel selector flip -> p95/p99 regression. Mitigation: revert + stronger onboarding invariants + better kernel selector fallbacks for borderline seq_len distributions.

maya: thanks all. I'll monitor the perf CI runs and post updates here. :thumbsup:

(added later) ci-bot: perf-ci: PR #1427 reverted commit 3f8a2d7. p95 back to 16ms, p99 back to 19ms on staging. Regression resolved.
